text:
Shale outcrop-Midway complex, steep (25 to 90 percent slopes) (SOc).
This complex is on deeply dissected clay shale highlands with 50 to 200 feet relief. The areas occur as a single, nearly perpendicular escarpment along a valley or as a number of closely spaced narrow ridges and drainageways at the head of a valley. Single escarpment areas include one or two, 5 to 7 feet thick sandstone ledges mixed with the shale. The complex consists of 35 to 70 percent shale outcrop and 25 to 65 percent Midway silty clay loam. The Midway silty clay loam is on the ridge tops, at the heads of drainageways, and on the lower 1/3 of the escarpments. The Midway soil has a profile similar to the typical one described for the series.
Surface runoff is rapid, the erosion hazard is severe. Erosion is active. Runoff waters carry large amounts of sediment.
This complex is suited to range.
(Capability Unit VIIe Dryland; Shale range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 4)
